# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles population estimates for 362 excavated settlements across Belarus, Ukraine and Russia (excluding the Baltic provinces) from the Late Roman period (250AD) to the First All-Russian Census of 1897 (1900AD). Arranged across six ecological zones - the European forest-steppe, the mixed and boreal forests, the Middle Volga and Kama-Urals, the open Pontic-Caspian steppe, the North Caucasus and Siberia - the tables trace how village life shifted when the Huns broke up the eastern Chernyakhov and Late Sarmatian settlements in the 370s AD. While open steppe camps and exposed southern border villages shrank or moved between 350AD and 450AD, fortified hillforts (*gorodishcha*), woodland river villages (*selishcha*) and terraced mountain strongholds grew steadily from the fifth to the tenth centuries AD, laying the urban foundations of early medieval Rus', Volga Bulgaria and the Caucasian frontier.

# Methodology

This gazetteer brings together 362 excavated Migration Period (c. 250-750AD) and early medieval settlements - promontory hillforts (*gorodishcha*), river-terrace villages (*selishcha*) and steppe strongholds - across the six regions of Belarus, Ukraine and Russia (excluding the Baltic provinces). Together they trace the shift of population from the open Pontic-Caspian steppe into the woodland valleys of the Dnieper, Oka, Upper and Middle Volga, Kama and North Caucasus.

For each site, population estimates across the Migration Period (250, 350, 450, 600 and 750AD) and the early medieval transition (900AD) are worked out from excavated house counts, fortified and open settlement areas and cemetery grave totals [@oblomskiy2016kolochinskaya; @krenke2019moskvorechye; @goldina1999drevnyaya; @gadzhiev2002derbent]. Dates before a settlement was founded or after it was abandoned are marked with a hyphen (-). Where an ancient hillfort or village grew into a lasting town or village on the same spot, its population at the First All-Russian Census of 1897 (1900AD) is given in the final column [@troinitsky1905perepis].



# Results



## European Forest-Steppe Settlements

Table \ref{tab:reg1-sites} lists 72 excavated settlements across the Seim, Psel, Upper Don, Oskol and Desna forest-steppe valleys, covering the Kiev, Eastern Chernyakhov, Kolochin, Penkovka, Volyntsevo-Romny, Borshevo and Saltovo-Mayaki cultures [@shchukin2005gotskiy; @oblomskiy2002dneprovskoe; @oblomskiy2016kolochinskaya; @sedov1999drevnerusskaya].

## Mixed and Boreal Forest Zone Settlements

## Middle Volga, Kama-Vyatka and Cis-Ural Settlements

## Open Pontic-Caspian Steppe Settlements

Table \ref{tab:reg4-sites} lists 20 excavated trading ports, winter camps, river-delta towns and Khazar brick and stone forts across the Lower Don, Lower Volga and Southern Trans-Ural steppe [@shchukin2005gotskiy; @botalov2009gunny; @kazanski2020steppe].
